content: Demeclocycline is a tetracycline antibiotic used to treat a variety of bacterial infections, including acne. It works by inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis through binding to the 30S and possibly the 50S ribosomal subunits. This medication is effective only against bacterial infections and does not treat viral infections such as the common cold or flu. Administration Guidelines: Take demeclocycline on an empty stomach, at least one hour before or two hours after meals, as directed by your doctor. Swallow each dose with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) and avoid lying down for at least 10 minutes after taking the medication. Avoid taking this medication with dairy products, calcium, magnesium, iron, zinc, antacids, or multivitamins, as these can interfere with absorption. Separate doses by at least two to three hours. For optimal effectiveness, take the medication at evenly spaced intervals. If prescribed for an infection, complete the full course of treatment even if symptoms improve after a few days. Drug Interactions: Demeclocycline may interact with live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine), reducing their effectiveness. Avoid co-administration. It can also interact with products containing aluminum, calcium, magnesium, iron, or zinc, which may decrease its absorption. Administer demeclocycline at least two hours before or six hours after such products. Other medications, such as retinoids (e.g., isotretinoin, tretinoin), may increase the risk of pseudotumor cerebri (benign intracranial hypertension). Avoid concurrent use. Demeclocycline may increase the effects of certain neuromuscular blocking agents (e.g., pancuronium, succinylcholine), leading to respiratory depression. Use alternative drugs if possible. Antibiotics like demeclocycline may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives. Use additional non-hormonal birth control methods during treatment. Side Effects: Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loss of appetite, headache, dizziness, and lightheadedness. diff), and photosensitivity reactions (exaggerated sunburn). Long-term use may lead to oral thrush or vaginal yeast infections. Demeclocycline may cause permanent tooth discoloration in children under 8 years old and during tooth development (last half of pregnancy through age 8). Avoid use in these populations. Special Precautions: Avoid demeclocycline during pregnancy as it may harm the unborn baby, including effects on skeletal development. It is also excreted in breast milk and may stain the teeth of breastfeeding infants. Patients with renal impairment should use lower doses to avoid systemic accumulation and potential liver toxicity. Demeclocycline may cause reversible dose-related nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (characterized by polyuria, polydipsia, and weakness). Discontinue therapy if this occurs. Patients exposed to sunlight or ultraviolet light should be advised of the risk of photosensitivity and discontinue treatment at the first sign of skin erythema. Contraindications: Do not use demeclocycline in children under 8 years old or during pregnancy unless absolutely necessary. Avoid use in patients with known hypersensitivity to tetracyclines. Monitoring: Monitor for signs of pseudotumor cerebri, especially in women of childbearing age who are overweight or have a history of intracranial hypertension. Watch for symptoms of C. difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD), which can occur during or after treatment. Discontinue unnecessary antibiotics and provide appropriate therapy if CDAD is suspected. Regularly assess liver and kidney function, especially in patients with pre-existing conditions or those on prolonged therapy. Additional Information: Demeclocycline forms a stable calcium complex in bone-forming tissues, which may temporarily reduce bone growth in premature infants. This effect is reversible upon discontinuation. Avoid prescribing demeclocycline in the absence of a proven or strongly suspected bacterial infection to reduce the risk of drug-resistant bacteria. Patient Counseling: Advise patients to avoid alcohol and marijuana, as these may exacerbate dizziness caused by the medication. Encourage patients to report any severe side effects, such as persistent diarrhea, vision changes, or signs of an allergic reaction, to their healthcare provider immediately. Demeclocycline is a potent antibiotic with specific indications and precautions. Proper adherence to dosing instructions and awareness of potential interactions and side effects are essential for safe and effective use.
